prompt:
Build the tenant policy compiler and migrate all sixteen resource gateways. The fixture is a dependency-free TypeScript monorepo with 80+ source/config/test files, a simplistic allow-list implementation and sixteen wire vocabularies. Use erasable TypeScript and .ts imports; add public regression tests.

Implement src/policy.ts with the exported types and Policy class. Rule = {id:string,effect:'allow'|'deny',resource:string,actions:string[],priority:number,conditions:Record<string,string|string[]|null>}; Request = {resource:string,action:string,attributes:Record<string,string>}; Decision = {allowed:boolean,ruleId:string|null}. Layer = {name:string,rules:Rule[],remove:string[]}.

Policy(layers:Layer[]) compiles ordered overlays. Each layer name and rule id is a nonempty string; layer names unique. removals are unique nonempty rule IDs; remove IDs first (unknown IDs harmless), then upsert rules by id. Duplicate rule ids WITHIN a layer or remove IDs within a layer are errors; a later layer may replace an id or reintroduce a removed id. A rule must have exactly the six Rule fields; layer must have exactly the three Layer fields. rules/remove must be arrays. priority is a finite integer, effect one of the two strings. actions is a nonempty duplicate-free array of nonempty strings; '*' is an action wildcard (other action strings match literally). resource is a slash-separated nonempty path with no empty segment. '*' matches one segment; '**' matches zero or more trailing segments and is allowed only as the last segment; wildcard characters in other segment strings are invalid. Literal segments may contain any other characters. conditions is an object: each key nonempty; each value null, a string, or a nonempty duplicate-free string array. Validate ALL layers, including rules later overwritten/removed. Reject invalid input with Error and never mutate caller data.

Policy.decide(request) validates a request (exact three fields, literal slash-separated nonempty resource with no '*' character anywhere, nonempty action string, attributes object of nonempty keys and string values). Match resource segments, action and ALL conditions: null means the attribute is ABSENT (own-property absence), string means equality, array means membership. Attribute inherited properties never satisfy a condition. Matching rules rank by descending priority, then descending count of literal resource segments, then deny before allow, then lexicographically ascending id using JS code-unit ordering. First wins. If none match return {allowed:false,ruleId:null}. Extra request fields or malformed attributes throw Error. Empty attribute strings are valid. A returned decision is independent of later operations.

Policy.replace(layers) validates and atomically replaces the entire compiled policy; failure preserves the previous policy. Policy.explain(request) returns ALL matching rule IDs in ranked order; Policy.exportLayers() returns a fully independent copy of the original layers in input order (not the flattened rules). Each method and constructor must own its data; replacing with no layers yields deny-by-default. exportLayers() is round-trip input for constructor.

Gateway integration:
Each gateways/<name>/vocabulary.ts exports wire names and defaultResource. Each codec.ts exports decodeLayer(raw) mapping vocabulary fields (layer/rules/remove, and id/effect/path/actions/priority/conditions) to canonical Layer and validating it. Missing remove defaults []; missing conditions defaults {}; ALL other required fields must be present and valid. Ignore unknown WIRE fields. Each gateway.ts exports create(rawLayers) with authorize(rawRequest), explain(rawRequest), reload(rawLayers), snapshot(). Wire requests use vocabulary.path/action/attributes; missing attributes defaults {}; other required fields must be present; ignore unknown wire fields. decodeRequest(raw) is exported from codec.ts. A gateway wraps ONE Policy; reload is atomic. src/api.ts exports gateways (all sixteen names), create(name,rawLayers), check(name,rawLayers,rawRequest) returning the Decision; reject unknown names. Preserve the vocabulary and defaultResource fields but do not silently default missing resource paths.

Migrate every gateway away from the old allow-list behavior. The public fixture tests only cover a one-rule allow case; hidden behavior follows exactly the compiler, overlay, validation, ownership and ranking contracts above.
